messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: /v1/chat elevated 502/504 errors originating from smart-routing (region: eu-west-1). Severity: potential customer impact. Please ack.
Priya: ack. taking this.
Priya: quick summary: we flipped a canary for model 'choir-rev2' at 10:11 UTC. Within 10m we started seeing increased retries and timeouts. Traces show fallback traffic cycling between variants.
Marco: I can see the spike. Tracing shows many requests hitting fallback selector then re-entering the canary affinity group. Looks like fallback picks "compatible" variant within same affinity bucket, not strictly stable.
Dan: grabbing recent routing config.
Dan: paste:
``````
routing_policy:
  type: rollout
  canary_pct: 7
  fallback:
    strategy: route_to_compatible_variant
  affinity:
    mode: sticky_customer
  region_preference: [request_region, global]
``````
CS-Liaison: two enterprise customers reported degraded assistant latency and occasional errors. They're throttling at client side now. Asking for ETA.
Eng-Prod: we started the canary from CI at 10:11:03 UTC.
Priya: evidence: repeated trace sequence: req=xyz -> choir-rev2@eu -> 504 -> fallback -> choir-rev2-standby@eu -> 502 -> fallback -> choir-rev2@eu ... repeated ~6 times, causing additional retries and capacity pressure.
Marco: this looks like an oscillation: sticky affinity + 'compatible_variant' that doesn't exclude canary family causes hot loops under load. Also noticed a tokenization mismatch warning in some fallbacks which explains some 502s.
SRE-Lead: recommended immediate actions: 1) pause canary, 2) change fallback strategy to prefer stable_release (choir-v1), 3) temporarily disable sticky_customer affinity OR relax TTL, 4) scale fallback pool in eu-west-1.
Priya: executing pause now: /rollouts pause choir-rev2
DeployBot: Rollout pause accepted (actor: Priya) at 10:24:18 UTC.
Priya: pushing emergency routing patch to override fallback selector -> prefer stable variant, and flip affinity to 'stateless' for routing.
``````
routing_policy_override:
  fallback:
    strategy: prefer_stable_variant
    stable_variant: choir-v1
  affinity:
    mode: stateless
``````
DeployBot: Hotpatch deployed cfg:hotpatch-421 by Dan at 10:27:03 UTC.
SRE-Lead: scaling eu-west-1 standby pool +3 nodes to reduce retries. Autoscaler triggered; nodes provisioning.
Marco: post-patch metrics: error-rate dropping, p95 latency trending down. Traces show fallbacks now going to choir-v1 stable nodes.
CS-Liaison: customer A reports significant improvement; customer B still sees a few failures but much better. They've requested a postmortem and rollback window for next canary.
Priya: root-cause hypothesis: fallback 'compatible' comparator matched by model family and affinity group. Because affinity sticky_by_customer pinned requests to the same affinity group, fallback sometimes selected a variant still tied to canary-capacity leading to repeated failures and a routing loop. Secondary bug: comparator didn't validate tokenizer/serialization flags leading to some 502s on standbys.
SRE-Lead: follow-ups and action owners: - Marco: tighten comparator to exclude canary-tagged variants, add tokenization compatibility checks. - Dan: add e2e test simulating affinity+fallback loops, create alert for >3 fallback cycles per request. - Priya: document manual pause/playbook and run tabletop. - CS-Liaison: customer comms, timeline for postmortem.
Priya: monitoring window: keeping paused until comparator fix + extra capacity validated. Will keep watch for 30m.
Dan: filing bug for comparator behavior: BUG-5921.
DeployBot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-2431 by Priya.
SRE-Lead: current status: mitigated (canary paused, hotpatch applied, autoscaled). Severity SEV-2.
Priya: handing off next 90m monitoring to Dan. Leaving notes in INC-2026-2431.
Dan: taking handoff. Will alert if regression.
CS-Liaison: customers updated. They requested weekly updates until fix is merged.
Priya: thanks team — will attach full traces and timeline to the postmortem.
incident-bot: Pager cleared. Incident state: mitigated.
